verses.115:1: {credidi}, por isso falei: * mas eu fui humilhado {nimis}.
verses.115:2: Eu disse, {excessu}: * Todo homem é mentiroso.
verses.115:3: Que retribuirei ao Senhor, * por tudo o que ele {retribuit}?
verses.115:4: {accipiam} o cálice da salvação, * e invocarei o nome do Senhor.
verses.115:7a: Ó Senhor, {quia} eu sou o vosso servo: * eu sou o vosso servo, e o filho da vossa serva.
verses.115:7b: Rompestes as minhas cadeias: ‡ a vós sacrificarei {hostia} de louvor, * e invocarei o nome do Senhor.
verses.115:9: {reddam9} {c9}: * nos átrios da casa do Senhor, no meio de ti, Jerusalém.

decisions.why: *Crédidi* is absolute here (no object), ἐπίστευσα; the line is quoted by St Paul (2 Cor 4:13, in DO's Latin reading *Crédidi, propter quod locútus sum*). The *crédere* row is *acreditar* (118:66 *acreditei nos vossos mandamentos*; 105:12 *acreditaram*) and notes that *cri* is the Latin's length but almost never said. Ruled: *Acreditei*, the row's verb. *Eu cri* is MS1932's wording and the form in which the Pauline quotation circulates (NVI *Cri, por isso falei*, seen in search titles) — it is the strongest option, kept as option 1. *propter quod* → *por isso* (DRB 'therefore', MS1932 *por isso*).

options.label: Acreditei
options.note: draft — the *crédere* row (118:66)

options.label: Eu cri
options.note: MS1932 *Eu cri, por isso falei*; the 2 Cor 4:13 form; *cri* is rare in speech

options.label: Cri
options.note: the Latin's length; a bare monosyllable at the head of the psalm

decisions.why: The *nimis* row has no single rendering; *sem medida* is the one used most with a verb (118:138, 45:2, 78:8, 106:38, 108:30), *muito* with an adjective (47:2, 92:5). *humiliáre → humilhar* (the row; 114:6 *fui humilhado*, the psalm this one continues; 118:107 *Fui de todo humilhado*). DRB 'humbled exceedingly'; MS1932 *estive na última humilhação* paraphrases. Ruled: *sem medida*, which also ends the verse on a paroxytone.

options.label: sem medida
options.note: draft — the *nimis* row with a verb

options.label: em extremo
options.note: a plainer adverb phrase; *muito humilhado* would need the order changed

decisions.why: ἐν τῇ ἐκστάσει μου — the same phrase as 30:23 (*in excéssu mentis meæ*), whose row the glossary says 115:2 can follow: *fora de mim*, the going-out said plainly. The Latin leaves open whether it is panic (30:23) or rapture (67:28a *em êxtase*); Augustine and the Fathers read the second here, DRB keeps 'in my excess', MS1932 *no meu abatimento extremo* decides for dismay. *fora de mim* keeps both open better than either alternative. The possessive is carried by *mim*.

options.label: fora de mim
options.note: draft — the row (30:23 *Eu, porém, disse, fora de mim*)

options.label: no meu êxtase
options.note: the Greek's word; heard as mystical joy, which decides the openness (cf. 67:28a *em êxtase*)

options.label: no meu abatimento
options.note: MS1932's reading; interprets

decisions.why: One verb twice, as the Greek (ἀνταποδώσω … ἀνταπέδωκεν): what shall I give back for all he has given back to me. The repetition is the Latin's (rule 2) and is kept, though God 'repaying' me is strange — the strangeness is the Latin's. MS1932 (*benefícios que me tem feito*) and the Brazilian Ordo (*por tudo o que me tem concedido*, fetched, `liturgical-use-brazil.md`) both drop it. The subject *ele* is named so that *tudo* is not heard as the subject of *retribuiu*. The head *Que retribuirei ao Senhor* is the Ordo's wording word for word.

options.label: me retribuiu
options.note: draft — the repetition kept; DRB 'rendered … rendered'

options.label: me concedeu
options.note: the Brazilian Ordo's sense (*me tem concedido*); drops the repetition

decisions.why: The *accípere* row is *receber* (open), with *tomar* where the subject takes rather than is given (74:3, 17:17). Here one takes up a cup to drink (λήμψομαι), and in Brazil *tomar* is also the everyday verb for drinking. *Tomarei o cálice da salvação* is DRB's 'take', MS1932's wording, and the Brazilian Ordo's (the priest's communion, fetched) — the one Latin-family form of this line Brazilian ears know. The CNBB's familiar *Elevo o cálice* is from the Hebrew (*esa*, lift) and is not followed. *salutáris* (genitive of *salutáre*) → *salvação* (D6). *Cálice* is off the cadence, as the row asks.

options.label: Receberei
options.note: the *accípere* row; makes the cup given rather than taken

options.label: Erguerei
options.note: DM1962 / CNBB (*Elevo*): the Hebrew's verb, not the Latin's

decisions.why: The *réddere* row names these two verses: *vota réddere → pagar os votos* (21:26, 49:14, 55:12, 60:9, 65:13), held against the stylist's *cumprir* twice (Pss 55, 60). The first colon repeats in 115:9 with only *coram* changed to *in conspéctu*, so the two verses are built from the same slots and differ only there. Natural order (verb first, D2), as 21:26 *pagarei os meus votos*.

decisions.latin: coram omni pópulo ejus … pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini … in conspéctu omnis pópuli ejus
decisions.why: The Latin uses two words in the same formula: *coram* (115:5a) and *in conspéctu* (115:5b, 115:9a). *coram → diante de* (55:13 row); *in conspéctu → à vista de* where it is the place of witnesses (21:26 *pagarei os meus votos à vista dos que o temem* — the same formula) and as a predicate; the *conspéctus* row names 115:5b *preciosa à vista do Senhor* as a test it passes. So 115:5a and 115:9a differ exactly where the Latin does. *Aos olhos do Senhor* (MS1932, and one of the two Portuguese forms of the line in circulation) is refused because *olho* is *óculus*'s; *à vista do Senhor* is the other form in circulation (Almeida-family Bibles, seen in search titles).

options.label: diante de … / à vista do Senhor / à vista de …

decisions.latin: pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini mors sanctórum ejus
decisions.why: Verbless, predicate first. The copula is supplied (D2). *Preciosa é à vista* puts *é* and *à* together (a hiatus the voice stumbles on); *é preciosa … a morte* is MS1932's build and plain Portuguese, and keeps the predicate at the head as the Latin does. Said alone as a versicle (*Pretiósa in conspéctu Dómini*, Commons of Martyrs) it reads *É preciosa à vista do Senhor*. *sanctórum* (ὁσίων) → *santos* (the row).

options.note: the Latin's order; the Almeida form (search titles); *é à* hiatus

decisions.latin: O Dómine, quia ego servus tuus
decisions.why: *quia* (ὅτι is not in Rahlfs here: ὦ κύριε ἐγὼ δοῦλος σός) gives the reason for what follows or precedes — 'because I am your servant (you broke my bonds)'. DRB 'O Lord, for I am thy servant'. MS1932 drops it. The Hebrew's particle is emphatic ('truly'), which the Latin does not say. Ruled: *porque*, leaving it open whether it leans back or forward, as the Latin does.

decisions.why: The *hóstia* row (open) is *vítima* (26:6b *uma vítima de aclamação*, 95:8 *Tomai vítimas*); it names this verse and says the two roots must differ from *sacrifício* (*sacrificáre* is here). Weighed against it: *hóstia* is the Latin's own word, MS1932's (*uma hóstia de louvor*), and here the Church reads the verse eucharistically (Corpus Christi Vespers antiphon *Cálicem salutáris accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis*, DO Pent01-4) — the 'wrong first hearing' the row feared would be, in this psalm, the liturgy's own. Ruled: the row, because a local exception here would make one Latin word two Portuguese words across 26:6b / 95:8 / 115:7b; *hóstia* is option 1 and is flagged in the glossary for Gustavo, since if he takes it here it should likely go to all three places.

choices.115:1: *ego autem → mas eu* (the *ego autem* row). *humiliáre → humilhar* as 114:6, the psalm this one continues (MS1932 prints Ps 115 as *Continuação do anterior*).
choices.115:2: *mendax* is an adjective with the copula understood → *é mentiroso*, supplied (D2). *Todo homem* without the article (Brazilian use; CNBB *Todo homem é mentiroso*).
choices.115:3: *retríbuam* (deliberative subjunctive) → future, as DRB and the Ordo; *pro ómnibus* → *por tudo*, number as grammar. The *retribúere* row: the bare verb is *retribuir* (it names 115:3).
choices.115:4: Second colon = 115:7b's third colon word for word, as in the Latin (rule 6). *invocáre → invocar* (the row; 114:3b *invoquei o nome do Senhor*).
choices.115:5: The inline marker (6) is not reproduced. The verse ends with a period where the Latin has a colon (the Latin runs on into 7a; a Portuguese colon at a verse end reads as unfinished).
choices.115:7a: The repetition *ego servus tuus … ego servus tuus* kept, with the copula supplied both times. *ancílla → serva* and the article, as 85:16 *o filho da vossa serva*. The *servo / serva* echo at mediant and final is the Latin's own (*tuus / tuæ*, *servus / ancíllæ*).
choices.115:7b: *dirúmpere → romper* (2:3 *Rompamos as cadeias deles*, 106:14 *rompeu as suas cadeias*); *víncula → cadeias* (the row, which names this verse). *sacrificáre → sacrificar*, *tibi → a vós* first as in the Latin (53:8 *sacrificarei a vós*). *laus → louvor*. **Accepted rhyme** *louvor / Senhor* at the second mediant and the final: the Latin has no such echo (*laudis / invocábo*), but both words are fixed — *louvor* by the *laus* row and the final colon by 115:4, which it must repeat word for word; no order of the middle colon removes it without a paraphrase.
choices.115:9: The inline marker (10) is not reproduced. *átrium → átrio*, *nos átrios da casa do Senhor* as 133:1b / 91:14 (*nos átrios da casa do nosso Deus*). Jerusalem, a single addressee who is not God, is *tu* (rule 3): *no meio de ti* (MS1932 the same).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (Latin, LXX, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Shared vocabulary with Ps 114 (in progress): *humilhar*, *invocar o nome do Senhor*, *ó Senhor*. Liturgical use in Brazil fetched and recorded in `liturgical-use-brazil.md`: the CNBB wordings are from the Hebrew; the Brazilian Tridentine Ordo's *Que retribuirei ao Senhor … Tomarei o cálice da salvação e invocarei o nome do Senhor* is the one Latin-family wording in circulation and 115:3a / 115:4 keep it. Hard readings: *in excéssu meo*, the doubled *retribúere*, *hóstia*, *quia* in 7a, and the *coram / in conspéctu* split in the repeated vow formula.

Hard checks pass. Soft flags accepted: 115:2 first colon −3 (*fora de mim* is the row's phrase; the Latin's *in excéssu meo* is long by itself) and second colon +3 (the copula *é* supplied and *mentiroso* is four syllables for *mendax*'s two); 115:5 first colon +3 (*diante de* for *coram*, the row); 115:7b middle colon +3 (*vítima* three syllables, *a vós* for *tibi*); 115:7b rhyme *louvor / Senhor* accepted for the reason in `choices` (two fixed rows).
